ai.description: This sea snake reaches 1 meter. It is pale yellow with 40–50 blackish dorsal bands. Key features include a small head, a compressed tail, and a distinctively keeled ventral scale row.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis mamillaris* is best distinguished by its very small head and a series of 25–30 distinct, dark, rhomboidal body bands that narrow significantly on the flanks.
ai.habitat: The Bombay sea snake inhabits shallow, coastal marine waters and estuaries along the Indian subcontinent, typically frequenting muddy or sandy sea floors.
ai.behavior: The Bombay sea snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively hunting for small fish among the seabed and coral reefs.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis mamillaris* is viviparous, giving birth to live young. While specific clutch sizes and breeding seasons in India remain poorly documented, it is ovoviviparous.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hydrophis mamillaris* is found in coastal waters along the western coast of the Indian subcontinent, primarily off the shores of Maharashtra and Gujarat.
